scope: Source/proof review only; no retirement/process scan/archive or payload hashing/execution. Root reports known v4 live identities absent; this review does not independently establish process inactivity.

findings.finding: A partial link transition can fail before the current payload is registered in staged, so outer pre-unlink rollback omits it.
cases: rename succeeds then initial fsyncdir fails
symlink succeeds then fsyncdir fails; internal catch leaves existing symlink and outer staged lacks entry
findings.required: Track the current transition before rename and reconcile exact identity/phase on rollback, or fully roll back inside link_payload before propagation. Preserve failed rollback as explicit incomplete rather than claiming restoration.

findings.finding: Previously readable busy references are discarded on a later PermissionError before matched is computed; an explicitly accepted unknown can consequently hide a known reference.
findings.required: Accumulate matches immediately after each successful observation; preserve them on later permission/disappearance errors; always refuse busy even for accepted unknown identities.

confirmedBoundaries.deletion: Manifest-listed ordinary files and known empty directories only; no recursive delete.
confirmedBoundaries.intent: Durable link/unlink intention before corresponding mutation; failure after unlink_started retains uncertainty and avoids hidden partial repair.
confirmedBoundaries.preservation: v4 absent from NAMES; proof is hash-pinned and copied roots exact. Receipt/cache/home/tmp/fixture paths not targeted.
confirmedBoundaries.verification: Reference, candidate and archive bytes are verified before unlink; source-review did not execute verification.

limits: The 180-second budget is cooperative between filesystem reads/operations; blocking open/read/fsync is not preempted by bound().
Root-coordinated no-launch window remains a prerequisite; cmdline/exe/cwd snapshot is not FD/maps or whole-machine inactivity proof.
Source assertions do not prove actual operation result or recovered storage bytes.
